title: Living Things Change Their Environment
seo_title: Kindergarten Worksheets: How Plants and Animals Change Their Environment
standard_text: Construct an argument supported by evidence for how plants and animals (including humans) can change the environment to meet their needs.
meta_desc: Free kindergarten science worksheets (NGSS K-ESS2-2): how squirrels, beavers, birds, worms, tree roots and people change the land to meet their needs. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_sub: Animals dig and build. Roots crack rock. People build too.
body_html:
How to think about it

Living things change where they live.

  • Animals dig and build homes.
  • Plant roots can crack rocks.
  • People build houses and farms.
Example

A bird builds a nest. Why?

It needs a home.

Answer: for a home

Example

A sidewalk is cracked by a tree. How?

Roots grow and push.

Answer: the roots

Common mistakes

  • Thinking only people change the land.
  • Thinking plants cannot change anything.
  • Thinking animals build things only for fun.

faq.q: How do animals change their environment?
faq.a: Squirrels dig holes for nuts, birds build nests, beavers build dams and worms dig tunnels.
Yes. Tree roots can crack sidewalks and rocks as they grow.

faq.q: Why do living things change the land?
faq.a: To meet their needs: food, water and a safe home.
